subject: Retention off-ramp runbook and log exceptions — MedSafe alignment
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: sara.dpo@medsafehealth.com, devops@medsafehealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention off-ramp runbook and log exceptions — MedSafe alignment

Hi Sara / MedSafe team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to make the off-ramp plan explicit in the DPA addendum so your audit team has a clear runbook for:
- scheduled backup purge timelines (primary + cross-region replicas)
- emergency deletion triggers and evidence capture
- short-lived log retention exceptions for forensic hold requests

Attached are two working artifacts: MedSafe_DPA_RetentionMatrix_v3.xlsx (mapping by data category and retention) and backup_purge_timeline_v2.pdf (proposed purge windows and escalation path).

Quick asks from our side to keep momentum:
1) Can you confirm any regulatory hold windows that would supersede our standard purge cadence?
2) Which internal MedSafe roles should be included on the emergency-delete approval path (name + email)?
3) Are there any active third-party subpoenas or litigation holds we should be aware of that would affect the 30/60/90-day purge bands?

We propose the following timeline to finalize the addendum:
- 10/19: MedSafe provides hold-role list + any hold windows
- 10/23: Redwood incorporates final retention matrix and sends for legal review
- 10/29: DocuSign turn-around target

If that works, we’ll route the DPA addendum through your procurement contact and set a one-hour review slot.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Programs, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: MedSafe_DPA_RetentionMatrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), backup_purge_timeline_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: sara.dpo@medsafehealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: devops@medsafehealth.com, procurement@medsafehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-17T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention off-ramp runbook and log exceptions — MedSafe alignment

Laura —

Thanks for pulling these together and for the clear timeline. A few items from the DPO / legal side:
1) Regulatory hold windows — for select PHI subsets we have a statutory hold of 7 years for patient records; however those holds apply only to identified patient records, not ephemeral inference logs. We will flag any customerspecific exceptions.
2) Approval path: 
   - Angela Park, Legal Ops (angela.park@medsafehealth.com) — contract sign-off
   - Mark Ruiz, Security (mark.ruiz@medsafehealth.com) — emergency-delete approval
   - Jamie Collins, IT Ops (devops@medsafehealth.com) — execution contact
3) We currently have one active litigation hold for a closed case that does not touch Redwood-managed retention, so no immediate change to purge bands.

On log retention exceptions — we need a documented maximum of 180 days for any short-term exception and a formal request / justification before we allow that extension. Can Redwood provide a minimal evidence package (audit log showing the request, timeline, and who authorized) when an exception is executed?

Happy to take the 10/19 deadline to provide any additional notes; procurement will coordinate signature.

— Sara D.
Data Protection Officer
MedSafe Health

Date: 2026-10-18T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention off-ramp runbook and log exceptions — MedSafe alignment

Sara / Laura —

Thanks for the clarifications, Sara. A couple of practical notes from ops as we translate this into the addendum and runbook:

1) Evidence package — yes, Redwood can produce an \"exception evidence bundle\": request form (who/why), ops approval ticket, purge execution log (timestamps + objects affected), and a signed approval email. We’ll add a template for that bundle to the runbook.

2) Purge bands — given the statutory note, we’ll map categories as follows in the matrix: 
   - Identified patient records: retention per customer instruction (we’ll surface a mandatory 7-year flag)
   - Inference artifacts (non-PII): default 30 days, 90-day tier for workloads you mark as extended retention
   - Operational logs: default 7 days, with an exception pathway up to 180 days when authorized

3) Backup purge timeline — ops recommends staggered purge windows to avoid cross-region reconstruction gaps. Proposed windows in backup_purge_timeline_v2.pdf: Primary region purge on Tuesday 02:00–03:00 UTC, Replica purge Thursday 02:00–03:00 UTC, final tombstone sweep Sunday 04:00–05:00 UTC. We capture cross-region barriers and manual approvals for any rollback within 72 hours.

4) Change control — we will add a 48-hour notification SLA to the runbook for any planned purge schedule changes and a 24-hour clinic for emergency deletes.

Next steps: Laura, can you fold these operational bullet points into the DPA addendum draft? I’ve attached a short ops checklist and will add the template to the internal runbook page (link in comments).

-Kimberly
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: 2026-10-19T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention off-ramp runbook and log exceptions — MedSafe alignment

Laura / team —

This looks good and I approve the operational approach with two caveats before we finalize the addendum:

1) For emergency-delete rollback: limit automatic rollbacks to a 72-hour window after purge and require manual authorization thereafter. That should be explicit in the runbook.
2) For evidence retention: we need to retain the exception evidence bundle for a minimum of 3 years for our internal audit trail (even if the data objects are deleted). Confirm that MedSafe is okay with Redwood retaining these audit artifacts (they contain request metadata, not substantive customer data).

If MedSafe confirms (2) — i.e., acceptance of a 3-year retention for the evidence bundle — then we can proceed to legal review on 10/23 and target DocuSign the week of 10/26.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Product Operations (serving runtime & platform)
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
